subject: Connectivity allowlist assurance — RFP follow-up
messages:
From: Ian Morgan <ian.morgan@oakridgeinc.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Connectivity allowlist and segmentation — RFP item 4.2

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking Oakridge's RFP. Item 4.2 asks for a clear description and evidence of how Redwood enforces connectivity allowlists between customer tenants, control plane components, and outbound services. Specifically, our security team needs:

- A network diagram showing permitted connectivity paths (control <-> inference worker, sidecar flows, egress destinations).
- A one-paragraph threat summary focused on cross-tenant lateral risk through network paths.
- Examples of logs/artifacts that demonstrate enforcement (VPC flow logs, firewall rules, or equivalent).

We know some of these may be redacted; that's fine. Can you provide diagrams and a short write-up, and indicate any operational controls (bastion, NAT, proxy) used for egress?

Best,
Ian
Ian Morgan
Security Architect, Oakridge Financial
ian.morgan@oakridgeinc.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Oakridge RFP — need diagrams + evidence (deadline Tue)

Team —

Oakridge asked for a short deliverable covering connectivity allowlists and isolation. They specifically want:

1) A simple network diagram that highlights which components are allowed to call each other (control plane, tenant control sockets, inference workers, sidecar proxies, external egress). Prefer SVG.
2) A one-paragraph threat-model focused on network lateral movement potential and mitigations we operate today.
3) Sample artifacts: sanitized VPC flow log excerpt or equivalent, and the egress policy doc.

Can you each own the following:
- Vanessa: canonical allowlist diagram + single-page legend (SVG)
- Karthik: short threat-model paragraph and a brief note on kernel-level hardening we reference
- Irene: sample flowlog and the bastionless-egress-policy.md (sanitized)

Deadline: EOD Mon (I want to assemble and send Tue morning to Oakridge). Keep the language client-facing and avoid internal-only acronyms. I'm attaching the overview I already sent.

Thanks —
Rachel
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-19T09:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Oakridge RFP — need diagrams + evidence (deadline Tue)

Rachel —

Attached: allowlist-network-diagram.svg (single-page, annotated), flowlog-sample.txt (redacted sample showing deny/allow hits), bastionless-egress-policy.md (high-level controls). Key points to call out to Oakridge:

- Tenant traffic separation: Each customer tenant is assigned isolated compute lanes with enforced network policies at the sidecar and virtual NIC layer; cross-tenant flows are blocked by default.
- Control plane interactions: Control plane APIs authenticate and are allowed only from managed control-plane subnets; agent heartbeats use mTLS and are filtered by allowlist.
- Egress handling: We use a verified egress policy that routes outbound destinations through an egress proxy cluster (no public-scope NAT allowed from tenant workers), with allowlist entries for cloud provider services and partner endpoints.
- Evidence: flowlog excerpt demonstrates a denied cross-tenant attempt and a permitted control-plane call (timestamps redacted).

Attaching artifacts now. Let me know if you want me to shorten the legend further.

V.
[Attachments: allowlist-network-diagram.svg, flowlog-sample.txt, bastionless-egress-policy.md]
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ian Morgan <ian.morgan@oakridgeinc.com>
Cc: Olivia Harris <olivia.harris@oakridgeinc.com>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-20T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Deliverable: Connectivity allowlist packet for Oakridge (RFP item 4.2)

Ian / Olivia —

Attached is the packet for RFP item 4.2. We kept it concise and client-facing per your ask. Contents:

- allowlist-network-diagram.svg — annotated diagram showing permitted paths between control plane, tenant workers, sidecar proxies, and egress clusters.
- connectivity-allowlist-overview.pdf — short narrative and checklist of enforcement points.
- bastionless-egress-policy.md — our standard egress control policy, sanitized.
- flowlog-sample.txt — redacted VPC flow log excerpt showing a blocked cross-tenant attempt and a successful control-plane call.
- redwood-allowlist-evidence.zip — (optional) compressed logs and rule exports with redactions applied.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Isolation model: multi-tenant compute lanes with network policy enforced at the network interface and sidecar proxy; default-deny posture for cross-tenant connectivity.
- Threat summary: primary residual risk is a compromised tenant process attempting east-west connections; mitigations include default-deny network policy, mTLS between control and agents, per-tenant KV and storage scoping, runtime sandboxing, and rapid circuit-breaker kill switches triggered from the control plane.
- Evidence: included flowlog sample and rule exports; we can run a live demonstration of a blocked attempt if you want.

Links and next steps: we uploaded the evidence bundle to a shared drive (link below). If useful, we can schedule a 30–45 minute walkthrough next week to step through the diagram and answer any engineering questions.

Shared evidence: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/OAK-2026/connectivity-evidence
HubSpot reference: HS-73421

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: allowlist-network-diagram.svg, connectivity-allowlist-overview.pdf, bastionless-egress-policy.md, flowlog-sample.txt, redwood-allowlist-evidence.zip]
